title: Manifest Destiny
objective: After this level you can explain how Texas, Oregon and the Mexican War added the West, and what that meant for the Mexicans and Native peoples already living there.
summary: Manifest Destiny claimed a right to the continent. Texas joined in 1845, Oregon was split in 1846, and Mexico ceded about 55 percent of its land. Many Mexicans lost theirs.

cards.headline: In a few years the US grew to the Pacific. People already lived there.
cards.body: Texas, Oregon and a war with Mexico remade the map in just a few years. What did the idea behind it promise, and what did it cost?

cards.headline: An idea with a name
cards.body: In 1845 the editor John L. O’Sullivan wrote of "our manifest destiny to overspread and to possess the whole of the continent." Believers held that spreading to the Pacific was the nation’s God-given right. Whigs attacked the idea as warlike and arrogant. For Native nations, as Level 41 showed, expansion had already meant removal.

cards.headline: Texas and Oregon
cards.body: Texas won independence from Mexico in 1836 and joined the United States on December 29, 1845. Mexico disputed the border: Texans claimed land to the Rio Grande, Mexico said the Nueces River. In the Northwest, settlers came on the Oregon Trail, and an 1846 treaty with Britain split the Oregon Country along the 49th parallel.

cards.headline: War, and a question from Lincoln
cards.body: President James K. Polk sent troops into the disputed land, and after clashes there Congress declared war on May 13, 1846. Not everyone was convinced. In 1847 Congressman Abraham Lincoln challenged Polk to show whether the spot where the first blood fell was really US soil. The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) ended the war: Mexico ceded about 55 percent of its territory, including California, for $15 million.

cards.headline: A promise on paper
cards.body: The treaty let Mexicans in the ceded lands stay and keep their property. But an 1851 law made Mexican landowners in California prove their titles, a slow, costly process. The cost of proving you owned your land was often the land itself.

cards.headline: Manifest Destiny
learned: O’Sullivan’s 1845 phrase claimed a right to the continent
Texas joined in 1845; Oregon was divided in 1846
Mexico ceded about 55 percent of its land in 1848
An 1851 law cost many Mexican Californians their land

questions.prompt: Put these events of Texas and the war with Mexico in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Texas won independence in 1836, Congress declared war in 1846, Lincoln challenged Polk in 1847, and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ended the war in 1848.

questions.prompt: Why did many Mexican landowners in California lose land despite the treaty’s promise?

options.label: The treaty ordered all Mexicans to leave California within a single year
options.rationale: The treaty let them stay and keep property.

options.label: An 1851 law made them prove their titles in a slow, costly process
They sold their ranchos to pay for the Mexican War
options.rationale: The 1851 law on proving titles, not war costs, took their land.

options.label: Mexico reclaimed the land after the war ended

questions.explanation: The cost of proving ownership under the 1851 law was often the land itself.

questions.prompt: Manifest Destiny claimed the continent for the United States. What had expansion already meant for the Cherokee?

options.label: A new treaty guaranteeing their land
options.rationale: New Echota took their land; most Cherokee opposed it.

options.label: Forced removal west to Indian Territory
Full US citizenship and a seat in Congress

questions.explanation: In 1838 the army forced more than 16,000 Cherokee west to Indian Territory.
